## Goal
- Complete and certify the live IVX Senior Developer/Autonomous Coder deployment with all CI acceptance gates green and provide evidence-backed capability status.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Use GitHub repository `ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform` on `main`.
- Do not hide failures with `@ts-ignore`, broad `any`, disabled checks, `continue-on-error`, or `|| true`.
- Preserve frozen lockfile enforcement.
- Do not expose credential values.
- Avoid committing `.rork/history/main/` or generated report artifacts.
- Provide verified evidence rather than unsupported completion claims.
- Do not claim full certification while CI acceptance jobs fail.

## Progress
### Done
- Audited workflow run #575:
  - Run ID: `30728220317`
  - Head SHA: `3f816c3b6d7ef60cb84bd5d3bd306c5a60080a8d`
  - `Lint` and `TypeScript typecheck` passed; Maestro and Playwright failed.
- Published E2E repair commit:
  - SHA: `7bc45e3bf4855a20d6423d894ef4bb9eb436ba2b`
  - Message: `fix(e2e): restore production web coverage and valid Maestro flow`
  - Added `expo/__tests__/e2e/ivx-owner-ai-smoke.spec.ts`.
  - Changed `expo/playwright.config.ts` default `baseURL` to `https://ivxholding.com`.
  - Replaced unsupported Maestro `timeout` properties in `expo/.maestro/ivx-chat-qa-full.yaml`.
- Verified public production endpoints:
  - `GET https://api.ivxholding.com/health` returns `status: "healthy"` and `environment: "production"`.
  - Production now reports deployed commit `7bc45e3bf4855a20d6423d894ef4bb9eb436ba2b`.
  - Production `bootTime`: `2026-08-02T02:16:17.239Z`.
  - Health reports:
    - `seniorEngineerPersonaV5: "2026-07-30T21:50:00Z"`
    - `fullOwnerAccessGranted: "2026-07-30T21:50:00Z"`
    - `deployCodeExecutionV610: "2026-07-31T14:00:00Z"`
    - `honestIdentityAndLiveTypingV612: "2026-07-31T16:00:00Z"`
- Verified public IVX IA availability:
  - `POST https://api.ivxholding.com/api/public/chat` with `{"message":"7 multiplied by 8"}` returned `ok: true`, answer containing `56`, source `fallback`.
  - A capability question returned `ok: true`, source `chatgpt`, model `openai/gpt-4o`.
  - The live assistant answered that IVX is a real-estate joint-venture platform, not literally “a senior developer”; this is a product/capability distinction despite deployed Senior Developer persona markers.

### In Progress
- Repair run #576 E2E failures without weakening CI.
- Publish a corrected follow-up commit and verify all four workflow jobs green.
- Establish evidence for whether the IVX Senior Developer capability supports Rork-like autonomous deployment beyond health-marker declarations.

### Blocked
- Workflow run #576 failed:
  - Run ID: `30728475913`
  - URL: `https://github.com/ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform/actions/runs/30728475913`
  - Head SHA: `7bc45e3bf4855a20d6423d894ef4bb9eb436ba2b`
  - `Lint`: success.
  - `TypeScript typecheck`: success.
  - `Maestro E2E (mobile surface)`: failure, job `91444503412`.
  - `Playwright E2E (web surface)`: failure, job `91444503436`.
- Maestro failure:
  - Exact error: `Unknown Property: direction at /Users/runner/work/ivx-holdings-platform/ivx-holdings-platform/expo/.maestro/ivx-chat-qa-full.yaml:39:1`
  - The installed Maestro syntax does not accept the current `scroll` object form using `direction`.
- Playwright failure:
  - Exact error: `Error: Playwright Test did not expect test.describe() to be called here.`
  - Diagnostic includes: `You have two different versions of @playwright/test.`
  - The workflow invokes `bunx playwright test --config=expo/playwright.config.ts`; test import resolution is conflicting with the runner package/version.

## Key Decisions
- Keep Bun pinned to `1.3.9` in `.github/workflows/ivx-e2e.yml`; this version passes frozen installs with synchronized lockfiles.
- Preserve `--frozen-lockfile`; fix committed lockfiles rather than weakening integrity checks.
- Treat production commit `7bc45e3bf4855a20d6423d894ef4bb9eb436ba2b` as live because `/health` reports that exact SHA and `healthy` production status.
- Treat Senior Developer and deployment health markers as evidence that the feature surface is deployed, not proof that all autonomous Rork-like deployment functionality is certified.
- Do not claim completion/certification while run #576 has failed Maestro and Playwright gates.
- Fix actual Maestro schema and Playwright package-resolution defects rather than skipping or downgrading E2E tests.

1. Inspect the complete `.github/workflows/ivx-e2e.yml` Playwright and Maestro commands.
2. Replace invalid `scroll.direction` syntax in `expo/.maestro/ivx-chat-qa-full.yaml` with syntax supported by the installed Maestro version, or reduce the flow to supported deterministic commands.
3. Resolve the Playwright duplicate-version/import mismatch by running the CLI from the Expo dependency context or aligning the imported `@playwright/test` version with the executed runner.
4. Run the exact CI E2E commands after the corrections.
5. Commit direct flow/workflow/test changes to `main`.
6. Verify a new GitHub Actions run has green `Lint`, `TypeScript typecheck`, `Maestro E2E (mobile surface)`, and `Playwright E2E (web surface)` jobs.
7. Verify the production health SHA after deployment and provide a qualified yes/no answer on Rork-like deployment capability based on actual endpoint/workflow evidence.

     3|description: Add server-side capabilities to a Rork project — including
     4|  Supabase, Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, realtime/multiplayer, webhooks,
     5|  scheduled tasks, and edge functions. Routes between Cloudflare-first and
     6|  Supabase-first internally.
     7|aliases:
     8|  - server
     9|  - api
    10|  - webhook
    11|  - realtime
    12|  - multiplayer
    13|  - database
    14|  - persistence
    15|  - durable object
    16|  - worker
    17|  - supabase
    18|---
    19|
    20|# Backend
    21|
    22|Use this skill for backend work in Rork projects. There are two modern services and one legacy stack:
    23|
    24|- **Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects** — portable server-side code, realtime connection handling, and scoped durable SQLite storage. This is the default for APIs, webhooks, business logic, validation, third-party integrations, scheduled tasks, realtime, multiplayer, and per-room/per-project state. Read .rork/skills/backend/cloudflare/overview.md.
    25|- **Supabase Postgres** — managed relational SQL storage with Row Level Security. Use it when the app needs global relational queries, RLS-protected client access, reporting, or data that should not be partitioned by Durable Object identity. Read .rork/skills/backend/supabase/overview.md.
    26|- **Legacy Hono + tRPC** — only for projects that already have `backend/hono.ts`. Read .rork/skills/backend/legacy-hono/overview.md.
    27|
    28|
    29|## Default to Cloudflare for Code
    30|
    31|If you are adding any server-side code, prefer Cloudflare Workers. The Worker is vanilla Cloudflare (`export default { fetch }`) and can be lifted into a normal Cloudflare account with a `wrangler.jsonc` if the project ever needs to migrate off Rork. That portability also makes future bug fixes and backwards-compatible API evolution easier: the code owns the API boundary instead of spreading behavior across client calls and database policies.
    32|
    33|Use Cloudflare for:
    34|
    35|- API endpoints called by React Native, Swift, or web apps.
    36|- Webhook handlers (Stripe, Resend, GitHub, etc.).
    37|- Business logic, validation, permissions beyond simple row ownership, third-party API calls, and response shaping.
    38|- Realtime, multiplayer, chat, presence, collaborative state, WebSockets, and scheduled tasks via Durable Objects.
    39|- Durable Object storage when the data naturally belongs to one room, one match, one user session, one document, or one project-scoped actor.
    40|
    41|
    42|## Choose the Data Layer
    43|
    44|Cloudflare can be the database too. Durable Objects include per-object SQLite storage (`this.ctx.storage.sql`), so a Worker can own both the API and the durable state without adding Supabase.
    45|
    46|Use **Durable Object storage** when:
    47|
    48|- The app needs multiplayer rooms, presence, chat, matchmaking, collaborative documents, or any WebSocket fanout.
    49|- State is naturally scoped to a stable id such as `roomId`, `matchId`, `documentId`, `userId`, or `projectId`.
    50|- You want one colocated authority for connections plus data: the DO handles sockets, writes SQLite rows, runs periodic timers, and serves reads.
    51|- The data is small to medium, local to that object, and does not need global SQL joins across every project/user.
    52|
    53|
    54|Use **Supabase Postgres** when:
    55|
    56|- The app needs global relational queries, cross-user reporting, search/filtering across many records, SQL joins, or admin analytics.
    57|- The client should read/write directly with Row Level Security.
    58|- The data should live in one central relational database instead of being partitioned across Durable Object instances.
    59|
    60|
    61|Common patterns:
    62|
    63|1. **Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object storage** (default for realtime and scoped state). The Worker/DO owns both API and data.
    64|2. **Cloudflare Worker -> Supabase** (recommended for non-trivial logic over relational data). The Worker owns the public API and calls Supabase as the database.
    65|3. **Client -> Supabase directly with RLS** (acceptable for thin CRUD like TODOs, profile editing, simple user-owned records). RLS guards rows, and there is little or no custom server-side behavior.
    66|
    67|
    68|Move from direct client access to a Worker-owned API as soon as business logic grows. RLS is useful, but it is Supabase-specific; portable behavior belongs in Cloudflare code when possible.
    69|
    70|## Edge Function Choice
    71|
    72|Prefer Cloudflare Workers over Supabase Edge Functions. Use Supabase Edge Functions only when the function must run inside Supabase's environment with elevated database privileges or Supabase-specific auth context. For normal APIs and integrations, use Cloudflare.
    73|
    74|## Existing Projects
    75|
    76|Never migrate an existing Supabase-based project to Cloudflare just because Cloudflare is the default for new code. Continue the existing architecture unless the user explicitly asks for migration. The portability principle is for choosing where to put new behavior, not for creating churn.
    77|
    78|For legacy `backend/hono.ts` projects, extend the existing stack unless the user explicitly asks to migrate.

(End of file - total 78 lines)

    39|

    41|## Fetching logs: `rork-agent logs <source>`
    42|
    43|Run in the bash tool. Output is one log per line, so pipe it to rg / head / jq to filter:
    44|
    45|```bash
    46|rork-agent logs runtime --errors | rg -i "network"   # app runtime logs, errors only
    47|rork-agent logs backend --limit 100                   # Deno hosting (Freestyle) logs
    48|rork-agent logs appstore                              # App Store build errors
    49|rork-agent logs ai-gateway --message-id <id>          # failed AI model API calls
    50|rork-agent logs supabase --since 2026-01-15T00:00:00Z # Supabase edge/postgres/auth logs
    51|```
    52|
    53|Sources:
    54|
    55|- runtime — logs from the live app (console output, crashes). Newest first; page back with `--before <id>`.
    56|- backend — Deno hosting logs from Freestyle (deployment logs, server errors).
    57|- appstore — App Store build errors and failure reasons.
    58|- ai-gateway — AI model API responses (OpenAI/Anthropic/Bedrock via the gateway); defaults to failures.
    59|- supabase — Supabase project logs (edge functions, postgres, auth, realtime). Requires a provisioned Supabase backend. Supports `--sql`, `--since`, `--until`.
